card.occupation: Branch manager at a builders' merchants (timber, plumbing and heating supplies) on an industrial estate between Sutton and Kirkby-in-Ashfield. She runs a staff of nine across the trade counter and yard.
card.education_detail: Left school in Sutton at 16 with GCSEs. Did a BTEC National in Business at West Nottinghamshire College and quit partway through the second year when a counter job came up. Since then she has done in-house management training and an IOSH Managing Safely course, and holds a forklift licence she hasn't used in years.
card.household: Lives with her husband Lee (41, self-employed electrician) in a three-bed semi bought in 2015. They have no children, which is mostly by choice and not discussed much. There is one elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Mabel.
card.cultural_background: White British. Born and raised in Ashfield, and her dad worked at a colliery until the pits closed. Christened and confirmed Church of England, and married at St Mary Magdalene's. She goes at Christmas and for funerals and would call herself Christian without making much of it. Her mum is still local and her younger brother lives in Hucknall.
card.professional_persona: Got the manager's job eight years ago mainly because she knew the stock and the trade customers better than anyone else, not because she wanted to manage. Blunt with staff and suppliers, doesn't do pep talks, and will tell a regional manager straight when a target is unrealistic. Scrupulously straight about stock counts and refunds and won't fiddle figures even when it would make her branch look better. Admin is her weak spot. Paperwork piles up, she leaves rota changes until the night before, and she relies heavily on her assistant manager, Dawn, to keep on top of compliance deadlines.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Walks Mabel round the reservoir most evenings and occasionally further in Sherwood Pines at weekends. Lee follows Mansfield Town and she has been to Field Mill a handful of times, but she finds the crowds a bit much and would rather listen to the result in the car.
card.arts_persona: Reads a lot of crime fiction on a Kindle and gets through series quickly. Likes Scandinavian dramas and true-crime podcasts on the commute. She hasn't been to the theatre since a school trip and isn't bothered about going.
card.travel_persona: Prefers quiet holidays. Most years they take a static caravan week at Mablethorpe or on the Norfolk coast. Abroad has been Lanzarote twice and a Tenerife trip for Lee's 40th. She dislikes airports and organised excursions and would happily go back to the same place every year.
card.culinary_persona: Plain cook and not especially fussed. Uses the slow cooker a lot (chilli, stews, gammon), Friday is chippy tea, and Sunday is a roast at her mum's every other week. Bacon cobs from the van outside the estate at work. Lee does more of the cooking than she does.
hobbies_and_interests: jigsaw puzzles (1000-piece, usually left half-done on the dining table for weeks)
pottering in the back garden with pots and hanging baskets
skills: deep product knowledge of building and plumbing supplies
handling awkward trade customers without backing down
spotting when someone's lying about a return
basic DIY: tiling, fitting a tap
card.career_goals: No big ambitions. She would like the branch to stop being short-staffed and to get through a year without a head-office restructure. She has turned down an area manager role once because it meant more travel, meetings and spreadsheets. Long term she would be content staying where she is until something better-paid and quieter comes along.
card.voice: Low, flat-ish Nottinghamshire accent, unhurried, with short answers by default. She doesn't fill silences and will just wait for the next question. Uses 'erm' when thinking and 'sort of' as a hedge now and then. Says 'tea' for the evening meal and 'cob' for a roll. The odd 'mardy' or 'knackered' slips out naturally. Will say 'sorry, what was that?' if the line drops. Not chatty but not rude either, just plain. If a question seems pointless she will say so, mildly: 'I don't really know what you want me to say to that.'
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and rarely bothers with capitals at the start of a sentence. Apostrophes are often dropped ('dont', 'its'). Minimal punctuation, sometimes no full stop at the end. Short answers, often just a few words. She doesn't proofread, so the occasional typo is left in. Doesn't use emojis.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit guarded, with little small talk. She can come across as curt or uninterested at first. She answers honestly, though, and won't exaggerate or pretend to know things she doesn't. She warms up slightly if the other person is straightforward and doesn't oversell anything.
small_things: the dog's arthritis and her expensive tablets
a trade customer who's been arguing about an invoice for weeks
the bacon cob van being shut on Mondays
the jigsaw that's been on the table since Easter
Lee leaving his tools in the hallway
deeper_things: mild guilt about not wanting children, and relatives who still ask
her dad's health since his stroke last year
feeling she ended up a manager by accident and isn't really suited to the people side
knowing she's disorganised and worrying it will catch up with her one day
a falling-out with her oldest school friend that she hasn't patched up
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam on a kitchen-diner table, angled slightly upwards, evening, lit by a warm overhead ceiling light that leaves faint shadows under her eyes. Head and shoulders are centred and slightly too close. Woman in her late thirties, pale skin with some redness on her cheeks, a neutral, slightly tired expression with her mouth closed. Dark blonde shoulder-length hair is scraped back in a low ponytail with a few loose strands. No glasses. She wears a navy fleece with a small embroidered company logo on the chest. Behind her: the corner of a white fridge-freezer covered in magnets and a vet's appointment card, a wall calendar showing the month, a clothes airer with towels on it, and on the right edge part of a dining table with jigsaw pieces scattered across it.
